brief.headline: Close the ₹8.48 L yearly price gap — PIK charges more than the best price we already pay.

priceAsk.summary: Match the lowest price we pay for the same items
priceAsk.target: ₹8.48 L saving per year (₹7.62/NOS on the main PET bottle SKU vs their ₹8.49/NOS)
priceAsk.basis: We pay TPAC ₹7.62/NOS and Suraj Blow Plast ₹5.24/NOS for the same bottles — PIK's prices are 11.5% and 2.6% higher. The open market also shows modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 per cap at higher volume.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Shorten payment to 15 days after receipt (from 30 days now)

brief.financialLeverage: PIK publishes no financials, so we don't know their profit, cash position or debt. That makes it harder to gauge how hard to push. Our ₹1.92 Cr yearly spend is meaningful to a private converter, but without their revenue we can't say how much. The plan leans on our own price data — we have proof TPAC and Suraj deliver cheaper — and on the strong alternates we've lined up, especially Manjushree (India's biggest rigid-plastic converter, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue) and three listed firms.

evidence.point: We overpay ₹8.48 L per year vs the best price we already get
PIK charges ₹8.49/NOS for the top PET bottle; TPAC delivers it at ₹7.62/NOS (11.5% cheaper)
Another bottle: PIK ₹5.38/NOS vs Suraj ₹5.24/NOS (2.6% cheaper)
Open market for 28 mm PP caps: asking ₹0.55–1.20/pc, with volume/spec flexibility down to ₹0.65–0.80
evidence.figure: askBand ₹0.55–1.20/pc, verdict: MARKET-FAIR; modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume / looser spec

evidence.point: Our current 30-day payment ties up ₹15.75 L; moving to 15 days releases ₹7.88 L
evidence.figure: ₹15.75 L working capital tied; ₹7.88 L freed at 15 days

evidence.point: PIK's finances are not public — we have no revenue, profit or debt figure to assess their room to move

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd (private, ₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100)
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter; makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms — the strongest second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd (listed)
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader for pails, containers and pharma packaging — strong and profitable backup for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd (listed, Pearlpet brand)
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist — direct fit for our PET bottle needs

risks: No published financials means we can't see if PIK is cash-tight or struggling — push too hard and a weak supplier might fold or cut corners on quality.
We spend ₹1.92 Cr with them but have no idea what share of their revenue that is — if it's tiny, our threat to walk carries less weight.
TPAC and Suraj are our price benchmarks, but we need to verify they can scale to cover PIK's volume if we shift orders — run a capacity check before the meeting.

The market backup leads (Reliance, Srichakra, IVL Dhunseri, Dalmia, Ganesha, Chemco) are not yet qualified — flag each as 'a lead to qualify (verify before RFQ)' and do not present any as an approved or priced source.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, but we're paying ₹8.48 lakh more per year than the best price we get elsewhere for the same bottles — let's talk about closing that gap.
